tasks.title: Add the agentkit-go sibling dependency to the module, container and CI builds
steps: Write TS-25-53 (reads go.mod, containers/hub/Containerfile, Makefile and the two workflow files as text from the repo root) and TS-25-54 (runs `go list -deps` for ./cmd/afc and ./internal/cli and asserts no internal/sandboxes or agentkit-go package) in internal/sandboxes/build_test.go; confirm they fail

In the Makefile build-hub-container target add `--build-context agentkit=../agentkit-go`

In .github/workflows/build-hub-cli.yaml add a clone step for agentkit-go next to the apikit clone

tasks.title: Load the [sandbox] section from config.toml with env expansion and unknown-key detection
steps: Write TS-25-1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 in internal/sandboxes/config_test.go (package sandboxes) and confirm they fail

Create internal/sandboxes/config.go with Config (provider, engine_binary, runtime, userns, max_ttl string, network_modes []string, Profiles []ProfileConfig) and ProfileConfig (name, default, image, cpus float64, memory_mb, pids, disk_mb as numbers that preserve non-integer input for later validation, network, ttl string, secrets, optional_secrets, env map[string]string, require_landlock); use toml tags and pointer/presence-aware fields where absence must be distinguishable from zero
Implement ConfigPath(): $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/config.toml when the variable is set and non-empty, otherwise ./config.toml

Implement LoadConfig(path) (*Config, error): return nil,nil when the file does not exist; wrap read errors and toml decode errors with %w; read with os.ReadFile and decode into struct{Sandbox *Config `toml:"sandbox"`} using toml.Decode WITHOUT expanding the whole file

Detect unknown keys via MetaData.Undecoded(), keep only keys whose first element is `sandbox`, and return an error naming the full key path (e.g. sandbox.profiles[1].memroy_mb; build the index form from the key parts), ignoring all keys of apikit-owned sections
Return nil,nil when the decoded file has no [sandbox] table

After decoding, expand ${NAME} in every string value of the section (scalars, list entries, env values) with os.Getenv semantics (empty when unset); a bare $ and `$5` stay literal; implement with a small scanner or regexp `\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}`, not os.ExpandEnv
Never include env values in any error produced by the loader

tasks.title: Validate deployment keys and profile identity, image and default
steps: Write TS-25-9, 10, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17 in internal/sandboxes/validate_test.go and confirm they fail

Create internal/sandboxes/validate.go with `Validate(cfg *Config) (*Validated, error)` that collects failures in a slice and returns errors.Join of all of them; Validated holds the effective deployment values (Provider, EngineBinary default "podman", Runtime, UserNS, MaxTTL default 4h, NetworkModes default ["none"]) and validated profiles

provider: required (message names sandbox.provider), "gateway" -> `sandbox.provider: the gateway provider is not supported by this build`, other values -> message naming sandbox.provider and listing accepted values (podman)
max_ttl: parse with time.ParseDuration, must be > 0, failure names sandbox.max_ttl; default 4h when absent
network_modes: each entry non-empty and unique, failure names sandbox.network_modes[i]
Require at least one profile (failure names sandbox.profiles)
Profile identifier helper: the profile name, or sandbox.profiles[i] when the name is missing; name must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$ and be unique (failure names the profile and `name`)
default: more than one profile with default=true fails naming `default` and the profiles; zero defaults is valid
image: required and non-empty, failure names the profile and `image`

Produce a ValidatedProfile type (name, default, image, resources, network, ttl time.Duration, secrets, optionalSecrets, env, requireLandlock) used later by the service; the fields for tasks 4 may be filled in task 4

tasks.title: Validate resources, network, ttl, secret and env names and report all failures together
steps: Write TS-25-18 through TS-25-27 in internal/sandboxes/validate_profile_test.go (TS-25-27 as a property test using testing/quick or a table of fault injectors over subsets) and confirm they fail
Resources: cpus must be >= 0, memory_mb, pids, disk_mb must be non-negative integers (a fractional value such as 1.5 fails); 0 is accepted; failures name the profile and the field
network: default "none" when absent; must be in the effective network_modes; failure names the profile, network and the rejected mode
ttl: required, ParseDuration, > 0, <= max_ttl (equal passes); failure names the profile and ttl
require_landlock defaults to false

secrets and optional_secrets: every entry passes internal/secrets.ValidateKey (failure names profile, list field and index); case-insensitive repeats within a list or across the two lists fail naming the profile and the repeated name; reserved names such as GIT_PAT are accepted
env: every key passes secrets.ValidateKey and must not equal (case-insensitive) a name in secrets or optional_secrets; failures name the profile, env and the key only, never the value
Ensure Validate still returns one errors.Join error containing every failure from the deployment and profile checks; keep error text value-free
Fill the ValidatedProfile fields that this task parses

tasks.title: Build and probe the provider, check capabilities and keep the validated service in memory
steps: Read the real agentkit-go source in ../agentkit-go (sandbox.Spec, Resources and the CPU field type, Provider, Capabilities, CheckSpec, podman.New/Options, local) and adapt names to it; note whether the CPU field is a whole number

Write TS-25-11, 28 through 35 in internal/sandboxes/service_test.go with a test-double provider (configurable Capabilities, recorded List contexts, failing or blocking List, counters for Create/Destroy) and a recording ProviderFactory; confirm they fail

Create internal/sandboxes/provider.go: `type ProviderFactory func(podman.Options) (sandbox.Provider, error)`, `BuildProvider(v *Validated, factory ProviderFactory)` passing Binary, Runtime, UserNS unchanged (defaults podman, "", "") and `NewPodmanProvider` using podman.New

Create internal/sandboxes/service.go: `New(v *Validated, p sandbox.Provider) (*Service, error)` that calls List exactly once with context.WithTimeout 10s, then checks every network_modes entry against Capabilities().NetworkModes (failure names sandbox.network_modes and the mode), converts each profile to sandbox.Spec (image, only fixed env, network, resources, TTL, RequireLandlock) and calls sandbox.CheckSpec once per profile; collect failures with errors.Join, each naming the profile and including the CheckSpec text
If the CPU field is a whole number, a fractional cpus fails naming the profile and `cpus`; if it is a float skip that check
Probe or construction failures return an error prefixed `sandbox:` that names sandbox.provider and sandbox.engine_binary and wraps the provider error with %w
Create `Start(cfg *Config, factory ProviderFactory) (*Service, error)` that runs Validate first and returns static failures without calling the factory or List, then BuildProvider, then New
Expose Service.Provider() and Service.Profiles(); never call Create or Destroy
Never put env values in any error

tasks.title: Serve GET /api/v1/sandbox-profiles from memory and keep values out of it
steps: Write TS-25-39 through TS-25-46 and TS-25-48 in internal/sandboxes/handlers_test.go using the harness from internal/merge/api_test.go (echo.New, /api/v1 group, test middleware reading X-Test-Auth into apikit.SetAuthInfo, httptest) plus the double provider from task 5; confirm they fail
Create internal/sandboxes/handlers.go with `RegisterRoutes(api *echo.Group, svc *Service)` where a nil svc means disabled; register GET /sandbox-profiles always

Handler order: apikit.GetAuthInfo nil -> apikit.WriteAPIError 401; nil svc -> apikit.WriteAPIErrorWithType(c, 404, "sandboxes are not enabled on this hub", "sandboxes_disabled"); PAT without read access (canReadSandboxes) -> apikit.WriteAPIError 403; otherwise 200

Define response types: {"profiles":[...]} with name, default, image, network, ttl_seconds (int64), resources{cpus,memory_mb,pids,disk_mb}, secrets, optional_secrets, env_keys, require_landlock; sort profiles by name; sort the three lists ascending and render [] (never null)

Build the response only from the Service's in-memory profiles: no provider call, no database or secrets.Store parameter anywhere in the exported API; never include env values, provider name, engine options or max_ttl
Property tests: random valid names for lists, identical body bytes for every authorised caller, env sentinel values absent from body, logs and errors across loaded/validated/started/listed runs
Update docs/api.md (new `Sandbox Profile Endpoints` section with schema and errors; add `sandboxes_disabled` to the error_type table) and docs/openapi.yaml (path, schema, tag, error type)
